title: ComponentQuery
description: A reusable, typed selection of the nodes in one scene that carry an exact set of component classes. Obtained from Scene.query; the same class tuple on the same scene returns the same query. A query selects; it runs nothing. Iterate it from a System, a behaviour or a scene hook: ```ts const movers = this.query(Velocity, Bounds); for (const [node, velocity, bounds] of movers) { node.x += velocity.x * delta; } movers.forEach((node, velocity) => { ... }); // no row array per match ``` A match carries every requested class exactly - a subclass instance does not match its base class. Disabled components and components of a paused or retained scene match; narrow with active, enabled, without and where, which return derived queries over the same index. Rows hold no `null`. ```ts // In init(): derived queries are built once and reused every frame. this.targets = this.query(Health, Bounds).active().without(Invulnerable); this.healthBars = this.query(Health).changed(); // In update(): this.healthBars.forEach((node, health) => bar.redraw(health.current)); ``` A change observer (changed) lists only the matches whose components reported a change with Component.markChanged, or joined the scene, since that observer last completed a pass - so each consumer keeps its own observer and none of them can take a change away from another. An observer stores one number, never a list of changed components, whatever happens between its passes. Each iteration works on the candidates that existed when it started: members added meanwhile are not visited, and members removed or destroyed meanwhile are skipped. Nested iterations are independent. A `for...of` iteration must finish within the frame it started in - resuming it after the frame boundary throws - and must not span an `await`, which the runtime cannot always detect. Each `for...of` row is a fresh array; forEach passes the components as arguments instead and allocates no row. Candidates come from an index per component class, never from walking the scene graph: an iteration visits the nodes of the rarest requested class and looks the others up on each of them.

members.name: active
members.description: The matches whose components are all Component.active. Cached: the same query each call.

members.name: changed
members.description: A new, independent change observer over this query: each pass lists the matches with a component that reported Component.markChanged or joined the scene since the observer's previous completed pass. Its first pass lists every match. types narrows which of the query's classes count; by default all do. A pass is consumed when it completes: a forEach, or a for...of that ran to its end. A for...of left early with break consumes nothing, so its next pass lists those matches again. A change reported while a pass runs is listed by the next pass, whether or not this one already visited the component.

members.name: enabled
members.description: The matches whose components are all Component.enabled. Cached: the same query each call.

members.name: forEach
members.signature: forEach(callback: (node: SceneNode, components: ComponentQueryComponents<T>) => void): void
members.description: Call callback for every match, with the node and its components as arguments in query order. Allocates no row per match, which makes it the form for per-frame loops.

members.name: where
members.signature: where(predicate: (node: SceneNode, components: ComponentQueryComponents<T>) => boolean): ComponentQuery<T>
members.description: The matches predicate accepts, called with the node and its components in query order. Not cached - build it once, outside the frame loop - and keep the predicate free of side effects: it runs for every candidate of every pass and of size.

members.name: without
members.description: The matches whose node carries none of types, by exact class like the query itself. Cached per class list: the same list returns the same query.

members.name: size
members.description: The number of nodes matching right now. Counts by visiting the candidates, so it costs as much as an iteration. Counting is not a pass: it consumes no change of a changed observer.

members.name: types
members.description: The requested component classes, in row order.
